item.description:
• Closing the last window now only hides it: clicking the Dock icon brings it back at once, with its tabs, graph and terminal, instead of loading every repository again.
  • When the window had really been closed, the Dock icon opened an empty start page instead of your repositories.
  • Pull requests no longer say GitHub rejected the saved sign-in when the repository's default account has an expired token but another account works: that account is skipped quietly, and accounts that need signing in are no longer picked by default.
  • Tokens are read from the Keychain once, so a busy Keychain no longer looks like a rejected sign-in.
  • The ⚠ next to a branch whose upstream was deleted on the remote explains itself when you hover it, and says what to do.

• First public release. Not notarized yet: on first open, macOS asks — System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Open Anyway. Later versions arrive through the app's own updater.
  • Commit graph for large repositories (100k+ commits), commit details and diffs (side by side or unified, word-level), file history and blame.
  • Staging by file, hunk or line; commits with amend, sign-off, signing (GPG/SSH), co-authors and team conventions.
  • Branches and tags, fetch / pull / push with upstream tracking, stashes, undo and redo for most operations.
  • Merge, rebase, cherry-pick and revert by drag and drop on the graph; interactive rebase; a three-way conflict editor.
  • Tabs, several windows, profiles that each keep their own tabs, recent repositories and commit identity.
  • SSH accounts that pick the right key per repository; GitHub and GitLab sign-in for pull requests, issues, reviews and Actions.
  • Built-in terminal, file editor, search and filters, worktrees, submodules, bisect, reflog recovery, Git LFS.
  • AI commit messages and explanations with your own provider; an MCP server so other tools can drive GitLoom.
  • Themes, layout and keyboard customisation; 16 languages.
